capas.problem:
6.5 PIN BEND ISSUE OCCURRED AT ENGINEERING TECHNOLOGIES
- DUE TO BEND PIN, MACHINING PROCESS CANT BE DONE
capas.why1: 6.5 PIN AREA NOT BEING MACHINED WHICH IS NOGO FOR FURTHER PROCESSES
capas.why2: PIN BENDING CAN CAUSE SUCH ISSUES AND 6.5 PIN MIGHT HAVE BENT DURING PRESSURE DIE CASTING PROCESS WHICH COULDN’T CAUGHT IN PRE DISPATCH CHECKING
capas.why3: PIN BEING BEND IS INHERENT IN MANUFACTURING PROCESS BUT QUALITY CHECKS FAILED WHICH CAUSED NOGO PARTS REACHED TO THE CUSTOMER
capas.why4: GAGE PROVIDED TO CHECK DOES NOT ENSURE IF THE PART IS 100% OK
capas.why5: IMPROPER GAGE ALLOWED DEFECT TO REACH TO THE CUSTOMER

capas.effectiveness: Die is handed over to customer permanantely
capas.problem: Major issue seen as a porosity across collar and Dia32 hole, which contributes approx. 80% of the rejection (casting rejection), Remaining 20% rejection occurred due to chip off, undercut, casting damage etc.)
capas.why2:
Trapped gas / shrinkage in die cavity
Air or vapour entrapped during metal fill
capas.why3:
Insufficient die venting / excess moisture in die
Steam generated from lubricant/water on die surface
capas.why4:
Excess release agent on die surface
Over-application of die lubricant per cycle
capas.why5: Manual spraying is operated instead of Auto sprayer

capas.effectiveness: Monitor the next 3 consecutive dedicated-vehicle shipments and verify that boxes are received by the customer without damage.
capas.problem: Customer reported that the packing box was received in damaged condition. The material was dispatched through ACPL Courier, and the damage appears to have occurred during transportation/handling.
capas.why1: Box was subjected to impact/rough handling during transportation.
capas.why2: Shipment was transported through a courier system involving multiple handling/transfer points.
capas.why3: Dedicated transportation was not defined as a mandatory control for this customer/part.
capas.why4: Transportation risk was not adequately considered in the packing/dispatch control. Packing and dispatch controls did not specify dedicated-vehicle transportation and verification of loading/handling conditions.
capas.why5: Transportation/handling through courier resulted in excessive impact/rough handling, causing damage to the packing box.

capas.effectiveness: Monitor the next 3 consecutive production lots and verify zero recurrence of the three defects.
capas.problem: During final inspection casting defects such as non-filling, soldering and chip-off were identified on the components. The defects were detected during the final visual inspection before dispatch, and the affected components were segregated to prevent unintended shipment to the customer.
capas.why1: Improper/unstable die casting conditions and die surface condition caused non filling,  soldering and oil mark.
capas.why2: Die temperature, metal temperature, shot/filling parameters, die spray/lubrication and die surface condition were not maintained consistently.
capas.why3: Process monitoring and die-condition verification were not sufficiently controlled during production.
capas.why4: Specific controls and reaction criteria for non-filling, soldering and chip-off were not clearly defined.
capas.why5: Inadequate process and die-condition control, together with insufficiently defined reaction controls for non-filling, soldering and chip-off defects.

pq_pfmea_templates.recommendedAction: Recount box; correct quantity; re-weigh; record correction

pq_pfmea_templates.detectionControls: Visual label check vs packing list; scan if barcode used
pq_pfmea_templates.failureCause: Label printing error; wrong template used; illegible thermal print
pq_pfmea_templates.failureEffect: Customer identification failure; wrong box opened on line; rejection
pq_pfmea_templates.failureMode: Incorrect, missing or illegible label applied to box
pq_pfmea_templates.function: Apply correct customer label on every box
pq_pfmea_templates.preventionControls: Label printed from system-linked template; 100% label verify before sealing
pq_pfmea_templates.recommendedAction: Reprint label; re-verify; do not seal box without confirmed label

pq_pfmea_templates.detectionControls: Visual check after packing; random box inspection before sealing
pq_pfmea_templates.failureCause: Parts dropped; no protective layer; rushing; no handling WI
pq_pfmea_templates.failureEffect: Cosmetic rejection at customer; rework cost
pq_pfmea_templates.failureMode: Casting surface scratched or damaged while being packed
pq_pfmea_templates.function: Protect castings from damage during packing operation
pq_pfmea_templates.preventionControls: Soft gloves mandatory; foam/paper liner in box base; handling WI
pq_pfmea_templates.recommendedAction: Inspect packed box; replace damaged parts; add protective liner

pq_pfmea_templates.detectionControls: Document check — delivery order vs packing list vs physical boxes
pq_pfmea_templates.failureCause: Similar-looking orders; manual process; no cross-check with DO
pq_pfmea_templates.failureEffect: Customer assembly stoppage; emergency recall; relationship damage
pq_pfmea_templates.failureMode: Wrong part or wrong customer order despatched
pq_pfmea_templates.function: Despatch correct material against correct delivery order
pq_pfmea_templates.preventionControls: Cross-check delivery order vs packing list vs loaded boxes before sealing truck
pq_pfmea_templates.recommendedAction: Stop despatch; re-verify all boxes; correct before loading; supervisor sign-off

pq_pfmea_templates.detectionControls: Document review checklist signed before truck loading
pq_pfmea_templates.failureCause: Documents not prepared in time; wrong revision; manual errors
pq_pfmea_templates.failureEffect: Customs hold; customer rejection; payment delay; audit non-conformance
pq_pfmea_templates.failureMode: Missing or incorrect documents — invoice, packing list, CoC, LR
pq_pfmea_templates.function: Ensure all despatch documents are present and correct
pq_pfmea_templates.preventionControls: Document checklist before despatch sign-off; system-generated packing list
pq_pfmea_templates.recommendedAction: Arrange missing documents; do not release truck without complete set

pq_pfmea_templates.detectionControls: Visual check of all sealed boxes before loading
pq_pfmea_templates.failureCause: Tape running out; no strapping on heavy boxes; no vehicle check
pq_pfmea_templates.failureEffect: Parts damaged in transit; customer complaint; replacement cost
pq_pfmea_templates.failureMode: Improperly sealed or poorly secured boxes in transit
pq_pfmea_templates.function: Ensure boxes are properly sealed and secured for transit
pq_pfmea_templates.preventionControls: Sealing check before loading; strapping on boxes >5 kg; vehicle dunnage check
pq_pfmea_templates.recommendedAction: Re-seal; re-strap; ensure proper dunnage in vehicle before departure

pq_pfmea_templates.detectionControls: Lot number check on label vs packing list before despatch
pq_pfmea_templates.failureCause: Manual lot tracking; no system link between production and despatch
pq_pfmea_templates.failureEffect: Loss of traceability; cannot isolate field complaint; audit failure
pq_pfmea_templates.failureMode: Lot number not recorded on despatch documents or labels
pq_pfmea_templates.function: Maintain correct lot number traceability through despatch
pq_pfmea_templates.preventionControls: Lot number on every label; recorded on packing list and invoice
pq_pfmea_templates.recommendedAction: Add lot number to label; update packing list; do not despatch without traceability

qualAlerts.containment: Hold dispatch through courier for the affected customer/part until the revised transportation arrangement is implemented. Inspect all ready-to-dispatch packing boxes for damage and adequacy.
qualAlerts.instructions:
1) Dispatch customer parts only through the company’s dedicated vehicle until further notice.
2 )During loading, do not throw, drag or drop the boxes. 
3) Before packing, check that the box is strong, dry, clean and free from damage.
4) Ensure parts are properly arranged inside the box to prevent movement. 
5) Close and seal the box properly with sufficient tape/strapping.
6) Ensure boxes are properly positioned and secured inside the dedicated vehicle.
7) Maintain dispatch records and photographs of the final loading condition.
qualAlerts.problem: Customer reported that the packing box was received in damaged condition. The material was dispatched through ACPL Courier, and the damage appears to have occurred during transportation/handling.

qualAlerts.containment: Segregate the affected lot, conduct 100% inspection for non-filling, soldering and chip-off defects, rework permissible parts, re-inspect after rework, and release only Quality-approved OK parts.
qualAlerts.instructions:
1) Immediately segregate all castings showing non-filling, soldering, chip-off or any abnormal defect. Do not mix defective/rework parts with OK parts.
2) Final Inspector shall carefully check the complete casting, with special attention to the affected areas shown in this Quality Alert.
3) Rework is permitted only when the defect is reworkable as per the approved rework method and does not affect drawing, dimensional, functional or customer requirements.
4) Only trained/authorized personnel shall perform rework. Use the approved tools and method. Do not remove excess material or alter critical features.
5) Every reworked part shall undergo 100% visual inspection of the affected area. Dimensional/functional inspection shall be performed wherever applicable.
6) A part may be released only when it meets all applicable requirements after rework. Mark/identify the batch or quantity as **REWORK OK** as defined by Quality.
7) If the part remains defective after rework, segregate it in the rejection area. Do not send it to the next process or dispatch.
8) Quality Supervisor shall approve the reworked lot before release. Operator self-approval is not permitted.
9) If repeated defects are found, immediately inform Quality and Production Supervisor. Hold the affected lot and verify die/process parameters before continuing production.
10) After die/process correction, the first-off casting shall be inspected and approved by Quality before normal production resumes.
11) Record defect quantity, rework quantity, OK-after-rework quantity and rejection quantity for traceability.
12) Only original OK parts and Quality-approved OK-after-rework parts may be released for dispatch.
qualAlerts.problem: During final inspection casting defects such as non-filling, soldering and chip-off were identified on the components. The defects were detected during the final visual inspection before dispatch, and the affected components were segregated to prevent unintended shipment to the customer.

1. Purpose

To ensure all incoming aluminium alloy ingots are verified for correctness, inspected for quality, and stored properly before being used in production.

2. Scope

All aluminium alloy ingots received at V R Alucast from any supplier.

3. Responsibility

Activity Responsible
Receiving and informing QC Store / Dispatch
Inspection QC Inspector
Accept / Reject decision Quality Head
Storage and issue Store / Dispatch

4. Procedure

Step 1 — Truck Arrives

  1. Store / Dispatch receives the truck and informs QC Inspector immediately.
  2. Do not allow unloading until QC Inspector is present.
  3. QC Inspector checks the delivery challan against the Purchase Order.
  4. Verify — Grade, Quantity, Supplier Name.
  5. If anything does not match — do not unload. Keep material on vehicle. Inform Quality Head immediately.
  6. If everything matches — allow unloading. Move material to the inspection area.

Step 2 — Visual Check

  1. Inspect all bundles and ingots before moving to store.
  2. Check for cracks, heavy scaling, contamination, unusual discoloration, foreign material.
  3. Check that grade marking and heat number are visible on each bundle.
  4. Check bundling is intact — no loose ingots, no mixed grades in one bundle.
  5. If visual check fails — attach RED tag to the lot and go to Step 6 immediately.
  6. If visual check passes — proceed to Step 3.

Step 3 — COA Check

  1. Collect COA (Certificate of Analysis) from the supplier.
  2. If COA is not provided — hold the lot. Do not proceed. Inform Quality Head. Contact supplier for COA.
  3. Check that the grade on COA matches the grade on the Purchase Order.
  4. Compare each element value in the COA against VRA-SOP-001 (Composition Specification) for that grade.
  5. Every element must be within the specified min-max range.
  6. If any value is outside the limit — attach RED tag and go to Step 6.
  7. If COA passes all checks — proceed to Step 4.

Step 4 — Spectro Analysis

  1. QC Inspector picks one ingot as a sample from the lot.
  2. Clean the surface of the sample before testing.
  3. Run spectro analysis on the sample using the in-house spectrometer.
  4. Record all element readings against the grade.
  5. Compare each reading against VRA-QA-003 for that grade.
  6. Every element must be within the specified limit.
  7. If any element fails — attach RED tag and go to Step 6.
  8. If spectro passes — proceed to Step 5.

Step 5 — Acceptance

  1. QC Inspector confirms all four steps are passed — challan check, visual, COA, spectro.
  2. Quality Head reviews and gives final acceptance.
  3. QC Inspector signs off the lot as accepted.
  4. Material is tagged as per the Alloy Grade Color Code document.
  5. Move material to storage. Follow Step 7 for storage requirements.

Step 6 — Non-Conformance (Rejected Lot)

  1. Attach RED tag to the entire lot immediately. Do not remove under any circumstance.
  2. Move the lot to the quarantine area — physically separate from all accepted stock.
  3. Inform Quality Head and MD immediately.
  4. Quality Head raises a Non-Conformance Report and contacts the supplier in writing with photos.
  5. Supplier must arrange replacement material or issue a credit note within agreed timeline.
  6. Rejected material must NOT be used in production under any condition.
  7. Only exception — written approval from MD for concession use, with documented reason.
  8. Update records with rejection details, date, quantity, and supplier response.

Step 7 — Storage

  1. Store each grade separately in the designated raw material area.
  2. Grade color tag must be visible at all times on every lot.
  3. Place ingots on pallets or wooden blocks — never directly on the floor.
  4. Do not stack more than 20 layers high.
  5. Storage area must dry, and clean at all times.
  6. No oil, water, chemicals, or foreign material allowed in the storage area.
  7. Only authorized personnel allowed in the raw material store.
  8. QC Inspector to physically verify stock, tags, and storage condition once every week.

1. Introduction

   This Quality Manual defines the Quality Management System (QMS) for V R ALUCAST – a high-pressure die casting business – and outlines the procedures and processes in place to ensure consistent quality in our products and services.

 

2. Scope

   This QMS covers the design, production, inspection, and delivery of high-pressure die cast products.


3. Quality Policy

   At VR ALUCAST, we are committed to delivering exceptional aluminum die-casting solutions that meet and exceed customer expectations. Our approach to quality is guided by the following principles:

  1. Customer-Centric Solutions
     We prioritize understanding and fulfilling our customers' needs with reliable, innovative, and high-quality products.
  2. Continuous Improvement
     We strive for excellence by continuously improving our processes, technologies, and skills to stay ahead in the industry.
  3. Precision and Compliance
     We ensure strict adherence to international quality standards, ISO 9001:2015 requirements, and customer-specific guidelines in every project.
  4. Team Empowerment
     We foster a culture of teamwork and accountability, empowering our employees to maintain the highest quality standards at every stage of production.
  5. Sustainability and Responsibility
     We aim to minimize environmental impact by optimizing resources and following sustainable manufacturing practices.


4. Organization and Responsibilities

   - Quality Manager: AKSHAY DAKE

   - Safety Officer: KESHAW KAMBALE

   - Production Operations: SAGAR SHIRGURE


5. Key Processes

   - Document Control & Procedures

   - Production Process Control

   - Internal Audits and Management Reviews

   - Non-Conformance Handling and CAPA

   - Supplier Evaluation and Compliance

   - Employee Training and Competency Management


6. Document and Record Control

   Refer to the Document Control Procedure and Control of Records Procedure for detailed instructions on creation, review, approval, distribution, and archival.


7. Continuous Improvement

   Regular internal audits, management review meetings, corrective actions (using 8D or fishbone diagrams), and customer feedback processes ensure ongoing improvement.

1. QUALITY INSPECTOR / TECHNICIAN

Reports To: Quality Head Department: Quality

Role in One Line: First line of quality control — responsible for checking incoming material, in-process parts, and finished goods to ensure nothing substandard enters production or reaches the customer.

Roles & Responsibilities:

  1. Inspect all incoming raw material — visual check, COA verification, spectro analysis — before it is accepted into store.
  2. Perform in-process inspection at the die casting machine — check dimensions, surface condition, weight at defined intervals.
  3. Perform final inspection on finished castings before they are packed and dispatched.
  4. Operate spectrometer, vernier calipers, gauges, and other measuring instruments correctly.
  5. Record all inspection results accurately on the same day.
  6. Tag accepted and rejected lots correctly. Move rejected material to quarantine immediately.
  7. Inform Quality Head of any rejection, deviation, or doubt without delay.
  8. Ensure all instruments are sent for calibration as per schedule and keep calibration records.
  9. Monitor and note process parameters during production — temperature, shot pressure, cycle time.
  10. Raise non-conformance reports for any rejection or deviation found.
  11. Participate in root cause analysis when rejections occur.
  12. Keep the inspection area clean, organized, and instruments in good condition.

2. QUALITY HEAD

Reports To: Managing Director Department: Quality

Role in One Line: Owns the entire quality system — from incoming raw material to customer delivery — and is accountable for product quality, process compliance, and driving improvement.

Roles & Responsibilities:

  1. Define and maintain quality standards for incoming material, in-process production, and finished goods.
  2. Review and approve inspection results, non-conformance reports, and corrective actions.
  3. Make final accept or reject decision on any lot or batch.
  4. Develop and maintain all quality documents — procedures, work instructions, control plans.
  5. Lead internal audits and ensure the plant is ready for external audits — ISO, IATF, and customer audits.
  6. Investigate customer complaints — find root cause, implement corrective action, respond to customer.
  7. Coordinate with suppliers on quality issues — rejections, COA discrepancies, repeated failures.
  8. Maintain and update the Approved Supplier List based on supplier performance data.
  9. Ensure all measuring instruments are calibrated and records are maintained.
  10. Work with Production Head to resolve process deviations and reduce rejections.
  11. Train QC Inspector and production team on quality standards, inspection methods, and rejection criteria.
  12. Report quality performance to MD regularly — rejection rates, customer complaints, audit status.
  13. Drive continuous improvement to reduce rejections, improve yield, and strengthen the quality system.

3. DISPATCH HEAD

Reports To: Managing Director Department: Dispatch / Logistics

Role in One Line: Ensures finished goods are packed correctly, documented properly, and delivered to the customer on time — every time.

Roles & Responsibilities:

  1. Receive dispatch plan from production and plan packing, labeling, and vehicle accordingly.
  2. Confirm with Quality Head that finished goods are inspected and cleared before packing starts.
  3. Oversee packing of finished parts — correct packing material, correct quantity, correct labeling as per customer requirement.
  4. Verify part numbers, quantities, and customer details on every consignment before dispatch.
  5. Prepare and check all dispatch documents — delivery challan, invoice, packing list, and any customer-specific documents required.
  6. Coordinate with transporter for vehicle availability and timely delivery.
  7. Confirm delivery with customer and resolve any delivery-related issues.
  8. Maintain finished goods stock records — what is in store, what has been dispatched, what is pending.
  9. Follow FIFO for finished goods — oldest stock dispatched first.
  10. Keep dispatch area clean, organized, and clearly segregated by customer and part number.
  11. Manage returnable packaging — trays, bins, racks — track and recover from customer.
  12. Report daily dispatch status to MD.

4. PRODUCTION HEAD

Reports To: Managing Director Department: Production

Role in One Line: Accountable for the entire production operation — planning, execution, output, efficiency, and machine health — while ensuring safety and quality on the floor.

Roles & Responsibilities:

  1. Plan daily and weekly production based on customer orders and delivery schedule.
  2. Allocate jobs to machines — 280T and 400T — based on part requirements and available capacity.
  3. Ensure production targets are met in terms of quantity and on-time output.
  4. Monitor machine parameters, shot conditions, and cycle times continuously.
  5. Coordinate with Quality Head on process parameters, rejections, and corrective actions.
  6. Ensure raw material is issued to machines correctly — right grade, right quantity — as per production plan.
  7. Manage die change, die maintenance schedule, and proper die storage.
  8. Lead daily production meeting — review previous day performance, plan current day, resolve pending issues.
  9. Identify bottlenecks and take corrective action immediately without waiting for escalation.
  10. Ensure all operators are following defined work instructions and safety rules.
  11. Monitor consumable usage — lubricant, hydraulic oil, shot sleeve — and raise purchase indent in time.
  12. Maintain production records — part-wise output, rejection counts, machine utilization, downtime.
  13. Coordinate with maintenance for preventive maintenance and quick breakdown resolution.
  14. Report daily production performance to MD — output, rejections, downtime, and open issues.

5. PRODUCTION SUPERVISOR

Reports To: Production Head Department: Production

Role in One Line: Manages the shift on the shop floor — operators working correctly, machines running on parameters, and any issue resolved or escalated without delay.

Roles & Responsibilities:

  1. Supervise all operators during the shift and ensure they follow correct work instructions.
  2. Check and verify machine parameters at the start of every shift — temperature, pressure, cycle time, lubrication.
  3. Conduct first shot approval at the beginning of every job and after every die change.
  4. Visually check part quality at regular intervals during the shift — do not rely on QC alone.
  5. Ensure raw material issued to each machine is the correct grade — verify color code before issuing.
  6. Record shift-wise production output, rejection count, and downtime accurately.
  7. Report machine breakdowns or parameter deviations to Production Head immediately.
  8. Ensure every operator is wearing required safety equipment — gloves, face shield, safety shoes — throughout the shift.
  9. Ensure die, plunger, shot sleeve, and tooling are in good condition before starting each job.
  10. Hand over shift clearly to the next supervisor — what ran, what issues occurred, what is pending.
  11. Maintain cleanliness of machines and work area during and at end of every shift.
  12. Flag any quality concern to QC Inspector immediately and stop production if in doubt.

6. OPERATORS

Reports To: Production Supervisor Department: Production

Role in One Line: Directly operates the die casting machine — responsible for running it correctly, producing good parts, and reporting any abnormality immediately.

Roles & Responsibilities:

  1. Operate the die casting machine strictly as per the work instruction for the part being produced.
  2. Check machine parameters — temperature, pressure, lubrication — at start of shift and record them.
  3. Apply release agent and lubricant to the die correctly — correct quantity, correct method, as instructed.
  4. Remove casting from machine carefully — no dropping, no striking against hard surfaces.
  5. Visually inspect every casting after removal — check for cracks, cold shut, short fill, surface porosity.
  6. Place rejected castings in the rejection bin separately — never mix with good parts.
  7. Perform fettling, trimming, and shot blasting as per instruction for each part.
  8. Count and stack finished parts correctly as per stacking instruction to avoid damage.
  9. Do not change any machine parameter without permission from supervisor.
  10. Report any machine abnormality immediately to supervisor — unusual sound, oil leak, parameter drift, die condition.
  11. Never leave machine running unattended.
  12. Keep machine and work area clean throughout the shift.
  13. Wear all required safety equipment at all times in the production area.
  14. Attend daily toolbox talk and follow all safety instructions given by supervisor.

1. Purpose

   The purpose of this plan is to establish a framework for responding to unforeseen disruptions and to implement strategies that minimize risks. This plan aims to reduce operational downtime, protect personnel and assets, and maintain quality and delivery standards in high-pressure die casting operations.

 

2. Scope

   This plan applies to all functions at V R ALUCAST, including production, quality control, maintenance, supply chain, safety, and administrative operations. It addresses potential disruptions such as equipment failures, supply chain interruptions, utility outages, safety incidents, quality deviations, and natural disasters, as well as outlines strategies to mitigate these risks.

 

3. Roles and Responsibilities

   - Quality Manager : Oversees the execution and continuous improvement of this plan; coordinates communication and corrective actions.

   - Safety Officer : Manages safety-related incidents, ensures emergency protocols are followed, and liaises with external emergency services.

   - Production Operations Manager : Supervises production-related disruptions, communicates with the maintenance team, and implements recovery measures.

   - Management Team & Partners: Provide strategic oversight, make critical decisions during extended disruptions, and allocate necessary resources.

   - Support Teams (Maintenance, Procurement, IT, etc.): Execute assigned tasks to restore and secure operations.

 

4. Risk Assessment and Identification

   Key risks and scenarios include:

   - Equipment Failure: Breakdowns of HPDC machines or auxiliary systems.

   - Supply Chain Interruptions: Delays or shortages of raw materials, especially aluminum ingots.

   - Utility Disruptions: Power or water supply failures affecting production.

   - Safety Incidents: Accidents, chemical spills, or material mishandling that jeopardize personnel safety.

   - Quality Issues: Process deviations or non-conforming products impacting output quality.

   - Natural Disasters: Floods, earthquakes, or severe weather disrupting operations.

 

5. Contingency Procedures

   A. Immediate Response

      1. Alert and Communication

         - Initiate the internal alert system immediately upon detection of an incident.

         - Notify the Quality Manager, Safety Officer, and Production Operations Manager.

         - Use the current emergency contact list for both internal and external communication.

      2. Safety Measures

         - Follow established safety protocols and evacuate if necessary.

         - Record incident details including time, location, personnel involved, and a description of the event.

 

   B. Equipment Failure and Production Disruption

      1. Initial Assessment

         - Identify the cause of the disruption (mechanical, electrical, or process-related).

         - Safely isolate and shut down affected equipment.

      2. Activation of Backup Plans

         - Engage the maintenance team to diagnose and repair faults.

         - Reassign production to alternative lines or machines when available.

         - Conduct an inventory check and issue quality alerts as needed.

      3. Communication

         - Notify suppliers regarding raw material issues and request expedited deliveries or alternatives.

         - Inform customers of potential delivery delays and provide estimated resolution times.

 

6. Mitigation Strategies

   To reduce the likelihood and impact of disruptions, the following preventive measures are implemented:

   - Preventive Maintenance: Regular maintenance and calibration of all production equipment, including weekly checks and cleaning.

   - Supplier Management: Maintain a diversified supplier base with regular audits and performance reviews.

   - Process Controls: Implement rigorous in-process and final quality checks and continuously monitor critical process parameters.

   - Training and Competency: Conduct periodic safety, equipment operation, and emergency response training for all personnel; maintain updated competency records.

   - Infrastructure Resilience: Ensure backup power solutions and redundant systems are in place where feasible; periodically review and update emergency procedures.

   - Communication Protocols: Establish clear internal and external communication channels for rapid information dissemination during incidents.

 

7. Post-Incident Recovery

   A. Incident Review

      - Conduct a root cause analysis using techniques such as 8D or fishbone diagrams.

      - Document the incident, analysis findings, corrective actions, and lessons learned.

   B. Implementation of Corrective Actions

      - Develop an action plan to address identified vulnerabilities and prevent recurrence.

      - Update procedures and training programs based on the review.

   C. Resumption of Normal Operations

      - Verify that corrective actions have been effectively implemented.

      - Gradually resume production once all safety and quality parameters are met.

 

8. Testing and Review

   - Conduct regular drills and simulations to ensure all personnel are familiar with the plan.

   - Review and update this plan at least annually or after any significant incident.

   - Incorporate feedback from drills and actual events into subsequent revisions.

 

9. Documentation and Record Keeping

   - Document all incidents, actions taken, and review outcomes in accordance with the Control of Records Procedure.

   - Maintain records for audit purposes and review them during management meetings.

Continual Improvement

1. Purpose

To establish a systematic approach for identifying, planning, implementing, and reviewing continual improvement initiatives across all processes and functions in V R ALUCAST to enhance customer satisfaction and overall performance.

 

2. Scope

This procedure applies to all departments and processes within the organization that impact product quality, customer satisfaction, efficiency, and compliance with ISO 9001:2015 standards.

 

3. Responsibilities

Role

Responsibility

CEO / Managing Partner

Approves improvement plans and allocates resources.

Quality Manager

Facilitates the continual improvement process and ensures documentation.

Department Heads

Identify improvement opportunities within their departments.

All Employees

Participate in improvement activities and suggest areas for improvement.

 

4. Continual Improvement Methods

The following tools and approaches shall be used for continual improvement:

  • Internal and external audit findings
  • Customer feedback and complaints
  • Root cause analysis and corrective actions (8D, Fishbone, etc.)
  • Process performance analysis and KPIs
  • Suggestion schemes and employee input
  • Benchmarking and best practices
  • Review of non-conformities and waste

 

5. Improvement Planning

Improvement opportunities are recorded in the Continual Improvement Register, and action plans are developed including:

  • Description of the opportunity
  • Responsible person or department
  • Resources required
  • Timeline for implementation
  • Expected outcomes

 

6. Implementation and Review

The assigned personnel execute the action plan. Progress is monitored weekly or monthly by the Quality Manager. Completed actions are reviewed to verify effectiveness and impact.

 

7. Documentation and Records

All improvement initiatives must be documented in the Continual Improvement Register, including:

  • Improvement ID
  • Date identified
  • Description of improvement
  • Actions taken
  • Results achieved
  • Status (Open/Closed)

8. Monitoring & Communication

Improvements and learnings are reviewed during Management Review Meetings. Significant improvements are communicated across departments to replicate successful practices.

17. FAIR COMPETITION AND ANTI-TRUST

V R Alucast competes in the market fairly, honestly, and in compliance with all applicable competition laws. Even as a small business, we are committed to ethical commercial behaviour.

·                  We do not participate in price-fixing, bid-rigging, or market-allocation agreements with competitors

·                  We do not discuss pricing, costs, or production volumes with competitors

·                  We do not engage in predatory pricing or practices designed to unfairly eliminate competition

Any violation of competition law can expose V R Alucast and individual employees to serious legal consequences. When in doubt, do not engage — report to management.

 

18. COUNTERFEIT PARTS

V R Alucast manufactures aluminium die castings to customer specifications. We are committed to supplying only genuine, conforming parts and will not knowingly source, use, or supply counterfeit or suspect materials.

·                  All raw materials (aluminium alloy ingots, consumables) must be purchased from approved and verified suppliers only

·                  Material test certificates (MTCs) must accompany all incoming alloy material and be verified before use

·                  No worker shall knowingly use sub-standard, substituted, or misrepresented material in production

·                  Parts that do not conform to customer specifications must be segregated and labelled — never dispatched

·                  Any suspected counterfeit or non-conforming material received from a supplier must be quarantined and reported to the Quality Manager immediately

·                  Customers must be notified promptly if there is any reason to believe a non-conforming part may have been shipped

·                  We do not relabel, re-stamp, or misrepresent part specifications, material grades, or inspection status under any circumstances

Supplying counterfeit or misrepresented parts is a serious breach of customer trust, a quality violation, and potentially a legal offence. It will result in immediate disciplinary action up to and including termination.

POLICY STATEMENT

V R Alucast is committed to providing a safe working environment for all employees. We believe all workplace injuries are preventable. No production target or deadline is more important than the safety of our people.

Our Goal: ZERO workplace injuries


1. RESPONSIBILITIES

Management:

  • Provide safe equipment and working conditions
  • Ensure adequate safety training
  • Provide PPE at no cost to employees
  • Investigate all incidents

Supervisors:

  • Enforce safety rules daily
  • Conduct toolbox talks weekly
  • Stop unsafe work immediately
  • Report all incidents

Employees:

  • Follow all safety rules and procedures
  • Wear required PPE always
  • Report hazards and incidents immediately
  • Never bypass safety guards
  • Look out for co-workers

2. MAJOR HAZARDS IN DIE CASTING

2.1 Molten Metal (680-720°C)

Risks: Severe burns, metal splash, hot surfaces

Controls:

  • Mandatory heat-resistant PPE (apron, gloves, face shield)
  • Keep area clear of water and wet materials
  • Never look directly into molten metal
  • Report all burns immediately

2.2 High Pressure Machines

Risks: Caught between moving parts, die closure

Controls:

  • Only trained operators on machines
  • All guards must be in place and functional
  • Never reach into operating machine
  • Emergency stop buttons accessible

2.3 Hot Dies & Surfaces

Risks: Contact burns

Controls:

  • Dies remain hot 30+ minutes after shutdown
  • Use temperature gun before touching
  • Warning signs on hot equipment
  • Heat-resistant gloves for die work

2.4 Fettling Operations

Risks: Flying particles, cuts, hand tool injuries

Controls:

  • Safety glasses/face shield mandatory
  • Cut-resistant gloves
  • Keep guards on grinders
  • Proper tool handling

2.5 Shot Blasting

Risks: High noise (90-100 dB), dust exposure

Controls:

  • Hearing protection mandatory (earplugs/earmuffs)
  • Dust mask when opening machine
  • Regular maintenance of ventilation

2.6 Material Handling

Risks: Back injury, crushing

Controls:

  • Proper lifting technique (bend knees, straight back)
  • Two-person lift over 25 kg
  • Use mechanical aids where possible

2.7 Hydraulic Systems

Risks: Pressure injection injuries, oil burns

Controls:

  • Never check leaks with hands
  • Report all leaks immediately
  • Lockout before working on hydraulics

3. PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE)

Mandatory for ALL Production Areas:

  • Safety shoes (steel toe)
  • Safety glasses
  • Earplugs

Die Casting Operators:

  • Heat-resistant apron/jacket
  • Heat-resistant gloves
  • Face shield (for melt handling)

Fettling Operators:

  • Cut-resistant gloves
  • Safety goggles or face shield
  • Dust mask

Shot Blasting Operators:

  • Hearing protection (earplugs + earmuffs)
  • Dust mask/respirator
  • Full coverage jacket

No exceptions. Violation = Disciplinary action

4. MACHINE SAFETY RULES

  • Never operate without training
  • Never bypass safety guards or interlocks
  • Keep hands clear of moving parts
  • Stop machine before cleaning or adjusting
  • Report defects immediately
  • Never distract operators
  • Emergency stop if anything unsafe

5. FIRE SAFETY

Fire Hazards in Die Casting:

  • Hydraulic oil leaks
  • Electrical faults
  • Hot work (welding, grinding)

Prevention:

  • Clean oil spills immediately
  • No smoking except designated areas
  • Keep combustibles away from hot surfaces
  • Regular electrical inspections

Fire Extinguisher (PASS Method):

  • Pull pin
  • Aim at base of fire
  • Squeeze handle
  • Sweep side to side

Evacuation:

  1. Stop work
  2. Walk to nearest exit (don't run)
  3. Assemble outside main gate
  4. Don't re-enter until authorized

Fire drill: Every 3 months

6. FIRST AID & EMERGENCIES

First Aid Box Location:

  • Production area (near QC desk)
  • Office area

First Aid Trained:

  • Manish Yadav (QC Inspector)
  • Irfan Sayyad (Supervisor)

Emergency Numbers:

  • Ambulance: 108
  • Fire: 101
  • Police: 100

For Burns (Common in Die Casting):

Minor burns:

  • Cool under running water 10-20 minutes
  • Report to supervisor

Serious burns:

  • Cool with water immediately
  • Call ambulance (108)
  • Cover with clean cloth
  • Treat for shock

7. INCIDENT REPORTING

Report Immediately:

  • All injuries (even small cuts)
  • Near-misses (could have caused injury)
  • Unsafe conditions
  • Equipment damage
  • Safety equipment failure

Procedure:

  1. Make area safe
  2. Provide first aid

Near-miss reporting encouraged - no blame culture

8. HOUSEKEEPING (5S)

Why Important:

  • Slips, trips, falls cause most injuries
  • Clean workplace = safe workplace

Daily Requirements:

  • Clean work area at end of shift
  • Clean spills immediately
  • Keep aisles clear (minimum 1 meter)
  • Return tools after use

Independent investigation conducted. Parties interviewed, evidence collected. Complainant consulted during process.

7-15 days (simple cases)
15-30 days (complex cases)

5. Resolution

Findings documented, corrective actions determined, decision communicated to complainant.

Within 30 days total from receipt

6. Implementation

Corrective actions implemented, monitoring begins.

As per action plan


Urgent Cases: Serious violations (safety risk, violence, severe harassment) are escalated immediately and investigated within 3-5 days.

Timeline Extensions: If more time needed, complainant will be informed with reasons and new timeline.

 

7. Confidentiality & Non-Retaliation Commitment

Confidentiality:

·        Complainant's identity kept strictly confidential

·        Only Grievance Officer and investigation team (on need-to-know basis) have access

·        Information not shared with anyone else without complainant's consent

·        Anonymous complaints: No attempt made to identify complainant

·        All records stored securely with restricted access

·        Breach of confidentiality is a serious violation subject to disciplinary action


Non-Retaliation Commitment:

V R Alucast strictly prohibits retaliation against anyone who:

·        Reports a complaint in good faith

·        Participates in an investigation as witness

·        Supports a complainant

·        Refuses to participate in unethical/illegal activities

Protected Actions: No adverse action such as termination, demotion, transfer, harassment, intimidation, or any unfavorable treatment will be taken against complainants or witnesses.

Consequences of Retaliation: Anyone found retaliating against a complainant will face disciplinary action up to and including termination, regardless of position.

 

8. Investigation Process

All complaints are investigated fairly and impartially following these principles:

·        Presumption of innocence until evidence confirms otherwise

·        Both complainant and accused given opportunity to present their side

·        Witnesses interviewed confidentially

·        Evidence collected and documented

·        Complainant consulted during investigation and before final decision

·        Focus on facts, not assumptions or biases

·        Completed within committed timelines

·        Findings documented in investigation report


Consultation with Complainant: The complainant (or their representative if they prefer) is consulted during investigation to clarify facts, provide additional information, and review proposed remediation before finalization.

 

9. Resolution & Remediation

Possible Outcomes:

·        Complaint substantiated: Violation confirmed, corrective actions implemented

·        Complaint partially substantiated: Some aspects confirmed, appropriate actions taken

·        Complaint not substantiated: No evidence of violation found

·        Insufficient evidence: Cannot conclusively determine, preventive measures recommended


Remediation Actions (if violation confirmed):

·        Disciplinary action against violator (warning, suspension, termination)

·        Policy changes to prevent recurrence

·        Training and awareness programs

·        Process improvements

·        Compensation or restitution to affected party (if applicable)

·        Environmental cleanup or corrective measures (for environmental complaints)

·        Termination of supplier/contractor relationship (for external violations)


Communication to Complainant: Complainant informed of investigation outcome, actions taken, and timeline for implementation. If anonymous complaint, outcome posted on notice board (without revealing identity).

 

10. Appeal Procedure

If the complainant is not satisfied with the investigation outcome or resolution, they have the right to appeal.


How to Appeal:

·        Submit appeal in writing (letter, email, or through complaint box) to "Independent Grievance Committee"

·        Include: Original complaint ID, reasons for dissatisfaction, additional evidence (if any)

·        Timeline: Appeal must be submitted within 15 days of receiving outcome

·        Appeal review: Independent Grievance Committee reviews within 15 days

·        Committee decision: Final and binding (unless escalated to external authorities)


Independent Grievance Committee Composition:

·        Management Representative (not involved in original complaint)

·        Employee Representative (elected or nominated by employees)

·        External Independent Member (if needed for serious cases - lawyer, HR consultant, social worker)

11. Grievance Register & Record Keeping

All complaints are logged in the Grievance Register maintained by the Grievance Officer. The register contains:

·        Unique Complaint ID

·        Date of receipt

·        Channel through which received

·        Type of complaint (Human Rights/Environmental/Ethics/Other)

·        Brief description (maintaining confidentiality)

·        Investigation timeline

·        Status (Pending/Under Investigation/Resolved/Closed)

·        Outcome and actions taken

·        Appeal status (if applicable)


Record Retention: All grievance records retained for minimum 5 years. Access restricted to Grievance Officer and authorized personnel only.

 

12. Awareness & Accessibility

Making the Mechanism Known:

·        This policy displayed prominently on notice board (English, Hindi, Marathi)

·        Copy provided to all employees during induction

·        Annual training session on grievance mechanism for all employees

·        Toolbox talks and safety meetings include reminders

·        Posters with complaint channels displayed in production areas, canteen, rest areas

·        Suppliers and contractors informed during onboarding

·        Information included in supplier agreements

·        Community stakeholders informed through local notices (if applicable)


Accessibility Features:

·        Multiple channels (phone, email, in-person, written, anonymous box)

·        Available in local languages (English, Hindi, Marathi)

·        No cost to complainant

·        No special forms required (though template provided for convenience)

·        Assistance available for those who need help submitting complaint

·        Working hours access and after-hours options (email, SMS, complaint box)

·        External channels provided for those uncomfortable with internal reporting

 

13. Types of Complaints Covered (Examples)

Category

Examples of Complaints

Human Rights

Discrimination, harassment (sexual/verbal/physical), forced overtime, wage violations, unsafe working conditions, child labor, denial of leave, retaliation, privacy violations

Unethical Business Practices

Other Complaints: Health & safety violations, quality issues affecting customers, violations of company policies, or any other matter affecting stakeholders' rights and wellbeing.

 

14. Annual Effectiveness Review

The Grievance Officer conducts an annual review of the grievance mechanism effectiveness and presents findings to management.


Review Metrics:

·        Number of complaints received (by type, channel, stakeholder group)

·        Average resolution time

·        Percentage resolved within committed timeline

·        Number of appeals

·        Complainant satisfaction (survey or feedback)

·        Repeat complaints on same issues

·        Accessibility assessment (are all stakeholder groups using it?)

·        Retaliation incidents (should be zero)

·        Systemic issues identified and corrected

·        Training and awareness effectiveness


Continuous Improvement: Based on annual review, improvements made to:
• Process efficiency
• Communication channels
• Awareness and training
• Policy updates
• Accessibility enhancements


Stakeholder Feedback: Periodic surveys or feedback sessions with employees, contractors, and suppliers to assess awareness and confidence in the grievance mechanism.

 

15. External Stakeholder Access

This grievance mechanism is available to external stakeholders including contractors, suppliers, service providers, and local community members.


Informing External Stakeholders:

·        Suppliers/contractors: Informed during contract signing, grievance contact details in agreement

·        Community members: Contact details displayed at factory gate, local language notices

·        Customers: Information available on request

·        All external stakeholders can use any complaint channel (email, phone, letter, in-person)

 

16. Protection of Complainants

Good Faith Reporting: Complaints made in good faith are protected even if investigation finds no violation. Complainants will not face any adverse consequences for genuine concerns.

Malicious Complaints: Intentionally false or malicious complaints made to harm someone will be subject to disciplinary action. However, unsubstantiated complaints are not considered malicious if made in good faith.

1.      Purpose & Scope

V R Alucast is committed to maintaining a safe, fair, and respectful workplace for all workers. This policy applies to all full-time employees, part-time workers, contract labour, trainees, and apprentices working at our die casting facility in Ichalkaranji,Kolhapur, Maharashtra.

This document establishes our commitment to upholding human rights and fair working conditions as per Indian labour law and internationally recognised standards.

2. Child Labour & Young Workers

V R Alucast strictly prohibits the employment of children below 18 years of age in any capacity. We comply fully with:

•      The Child Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016

•      The Factories Act, 1948 — governing employment of young persons

All new hires are required to present a valid age proof (Aadhaar card, birth certificate, or school leaving certificate) before joining. No exceptions will be made.

 

3. Wages & Benefits

All workers at V R Alucast receive wages that are at least equal to the applicable Minimum Wages set by the Government of Maharashtra. Our commitment includes:

  • Wages paid on or before the 7th of each month
  • Overtime calculated and paid as per the Factories Act, 1948 — at twice the ordinary rate of wages, applicable only when a worker exceeds 9 hours in a day or 48 hours in a week
  • Statutory deductions (PF, ESIC) processed and deposited on time
  • Payslips provided to all permanent employees
  • No unauthorised deductions from wages under any circumstances

 

4. Working Hours

Our plant operates on double shifts across approximately 26 working days per month. Working hours are structured as follows:

  • Each shift is 8 hours, inclusive of a 30-minute meal break, in line with the Factories Act, 1948
  • Total working hours do not exceed 48 hours per week per worker
  • Overtime is not a regular or expected part of employment at V R Alucast
  • In exceptional operational situations, overtime may be required with prior notice; it will be compensated as per the Factories Act
  • Weekly rest day ensured for all workers — minimum 1 day off in every 7 days
  • Shift schedule communicated in advance to allow adequate rest between shifts
  • No worker is pressured to work beyond their scheduled shift as a condition of continued employment

 

5. Modern Slavery, Forced Labour & Human Trafficking

V R Alucast has zero tolerance for forced labour, bonded labour, slavery, or human trafficking in any form. Our commitments include:

•      Employment is always voluntary — workers are free to resign with appropriate notice

•      No advance wage deductions used as a means of binding workers

•      Workers' identity documents (Aadhaar, PAN) are never retained by the company

•      No fees are charged to workers for recruitment or employment

 

6. Ethical Recruiting

All recruitment at V R Alucast is conducted transparently and ethically:

•      Job roles, responsibilities, wages, and working conditions are communicated clearly before hiring

•      No false promises or misleading information is given to job applicants

•      Workers are not recruited through illegal or unlicensed contractors

•      Recruitment through word of mouth or direct applications is preferred

 

7. Freedom of Association & Collective Bargaining

V R Alucast respects the right of workers to associate freely and raise grievances. As a small unit, we maintain an open-door policy:

•      Workers can approach management directly with concerns without fear of retaliation

•      Workers' rights to form or join associations are not restricted

•      Regular worker-management communication is maintained through monthly meetings

 

8. Non-Discrimination & Anti-Harassment

We maintain a workplace free from discrimination, harassment, and intimidation. The following are strictly prohibited:

•      Discrimination in hiring, wages, promotions, or termination based on caste, religion, gender, age, disability, or regional origin

•      Verbal, physical, or sexual harassment of any kind

•      Bullying or intimidation by supervisors or colleagues

Any worker who experiences or witnesses such conduct should report it immediately to the owner/proprietor. Complaints will be handled with confidentiality and fairness.

 

9. Women's Rights

V R Alucast is committed to providing a safe and respectful environment for female workers:

•      Compliance with the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition & Redressal)

•      Equal pay for equal work regardless of gender

•      Maternity benefits as applicable

•      Safe working conditions including adequate sanitation facilities

 

10. Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

We believe a diverse team strengthens our business. We are committed to:

•      Hiring and retaining workers from diverse backgrounds without bias

•      Providing equal opportunities for skill development and advancement to all workers

•      Treating every worker from machine operators to supervisors with equal dignity and respect

 

11. Rights of Minorities & Marginalised Communities

V R Alucast does not discriminate against any worker on the basis of their caste, tribe, religious minority status, or community. We ensure:

•      Equal treatment and opportunities for all regardless of background

•      No tolerance for casteist remarks, slurs, or discriminatory behaviour on the shop floor

 

12. Land, Water & Environmental Responsibility

Our operations are conducted from an established, owned facility. We do not engage in any activities that involve forced eviction or unlawful use of others' land, forest, or water resources. We follow all applicable environmental regulations for effluent and waste disposal from our die casting operations.

 

13. Use of Security Personnel

Where security personnel are employed at our facility, they are instructed to:

•      Conduct themselves professionally and with respect towards all workers and visitors

•      Not use force except in genuine emergency situations

•      Not be used to suppress workers' rights or legitimate grievances

 

14. Training & Awareness

V R Alucast will conduct basic awareness training on human rights and working conditions for all employees. Training will include:

•      Orientation for new joiners covering this policy and their rights

•      Annual refresher communication to all existing staff

•      Supervisors briefed on non-discrimination and anti-harassment obligations

Training will be conducted in Marathi and/or Hindi to ensure full comprehension by all workers.


15. Grievance Mechanism

Any worker who believes their rights have been violated can raise a grievance as per Grievance Policy procedure

 

16. Policy Review & Compliance

This policy will be reviewed annually or whenever there is a significant change in applicable law or business operations. The owner/proprietor is responsible for ensuring this policy is implemented and updated as needed.

  1. कृसिबल एका कोरड्या व ओलावा मुक्त क्षेत्रावर प्लास्टिक पिशवीत ठेवा. ओलावा धरल्यास ते खराब होत जाते.
  2. कृसिबल चे नुकसान टाळण्यासाठी योग्य रीतीने हाताळले पाहिजे. मिसहँडलिंग मुळे हेअर लाईन क्रॅक होऊ शकतो ज्यामुळे कृसिबल फर्नेस मध्ये ठेवल्यानंतर फेल होऊ शकतो.
  3. कृसिबल भट्टीमध्ये व्यवस्थित बसवलेले असले पाहिजे आणि ब्रिक व कृसिबल यांच्यामध्ये कमीत 3-5 mm च्या अंतरावर पाहिजे.
  4. सुरुवातीला कृसिबल नवीन असतो तेव्हा तो लाल होईपर्यंत म्हणजे 900 डिग्री पर्यंत गरम करणे.
  5. धातूला कृसिबल मध्ये सरळ उभे लोडिंग करणे आवश्यक आहे. धातू कृसिबल मध्ये घालण्याआधी फ्लक्स घालू नये. यामुळे कृसिबल जलद पातळ होऊ शकतो त्याच्यामुळे त्याचे आयु कमी होऊ शकते.
  6. कृसिबल मध्ये धातू रसाला थंड होऊ देऊ नये. गरम असतानाच ते काढून घेणे गरजेचे आहे. तसे न केल्यास कृसिबल तुटू शकते.

SOP for Die Preparation
(डाय तयारी संबंधीची सूचना)

 

1. Purpose

To ensure the proper preparation of dies before the start of production to prevent any defects and ensure smooth operations.

 

2. Scope

This procedure applies to all die preparation activities at V R ALUCAST.

 

3. Responsibilities

  • Die Department: Responsible for retrieving the dies as per the production schedule and ensuring they are clean and ready for use.
  • Maintenance Supervisor: Ensure all hydraulic and water connections are intact and that the die is properly maintained.
  • Production Supervisor: Oversee the die preparation process, including setting limits and temperature checks before production begins.

 

4. Procedure

  1. प्रोडक्शन शेड्युलनुसार डाय डिपार्टमेंट मधून डाय मागून घेणे.
  2. डाय आल्यानंतर ती स्वच्छ करून घेणे.
  3. त्यानंतर त्या डाय चे सर्व कनेक्शन्स (हायड्रोलिक व वॉटर) सुस्थितीत असण्याची खात्री करून घेणे.
  4. डायच्या कोर पिन्स, इजेक्टर पिन्स सुस्थितीत असल्याची खात्री करून घेणे.
  5. डाय च्या लिमिट स्विच चे कोर (इन/आऊट) असेंबल व सूस्थितीत असल्याची खात्री करावी.
  6. डाय च्या लिमिट स्विच चे सेटिंग्स योग्य प्रकारे करून घेणे.
  7. डाय सरफेस (मशीन platen वर रेस्ट होणारा) स्वच्छ करून घ्यावा.
  8. डायचा प्रिव्हेंटिव्ह मेंटेनन्स झालेला डेटा, डाय हिस्टरी कार्ड मध्ये रेकॉर्ड झाल्याची खात्री करावी.
  9. तसेच डायलॉग रस्ट प्रिव्हेंटिव्ह ऑइल लावून घेणे.
  10. डाय मशीन वर बसवण्यासाठी I-Bolts व्यवस्थित व न हलणारे असावे.
  11. डाय मशीन वर बसवताना EOT क्रेनचा वापर करावा.
  12. प्रोडक्शन चालू करण्यापूर्वी डाय टेंपरेचर तपासा.

SOP for Raw Material Storage (अलॉय ची साठवणूक)

 

1. Purpose
To define the standard procedure for receiving, color coding, storing, and issuing aluminum alloy ingots to ensure proper traceability, quality, and inventory control.

 

2. Scope
Applicable to all raw material (aluminum alloy) handling activities at V R ALUCAST from receipt to issue for production.

 

3. Responsibilities

  • Store Supervisor: Ensures all incoming alloys are verified, coded, stored, and recorded.
  • Quality Inspector: Verifies the alloy grade through spectro check before acceptance.
  • Operators: Follow FIFO and proper handling procedures.

 

4. Procedure

  1. ⁠⁠स्पेक्ट्रोमिटर वापरून आलेल्या ॲल्युमिनियम अलॉय चा ग्रेड तपासा.
  2. ⁠⁠तपासलेले अलॉय ग्रेड प्रमाणे कलर कोडिंग करा. (कलर कोड चार्ट वापरा)
  3. ⁠⁠कलर कोडिंग केलेले अलॉय निर्धारित ठिकाणी व्यवस्थित साठवा.
  4. ⁠⁠अलॉय ओलसर होणार नाही याची दक्षता घ्या.
  5. ⁠⁠मटेरियल इश्यू करताना FIFO (First In First Out) वापरा.
  6. ⁠⁠प्रत्येक अलॉयवर आयडेंटिफिकेशन लेबल असावे आणि साठवण व्यवस्थित रचनेत असावी.
  7. ⁠⁠मटेरियल नेहमी स्वच्छ व धुळीपासून दूर ठेवा.
  8. ⁠⁠दररोज आलेल्या आणि गेलेल्या अलॉयची नोंद स्टोअर रजिस्टरमध्ये ठेवा.

SOP for HPDC Machine Operation (मशिन चालविण्याची प्रक्रिया)

 

1. Purpose
To establish a standardized process for operating High Pressure Die Casting (HPDC) machines to ensure safe, efficient, and defect-free production.

 

2. Scope
This procedure applies to all HPDC machine operators at V R ALUCAST during all production shifts.

 

3. Responsibilities

  • Machine Operator: Follow each step in the operation process to ensure safe and quality production.
  • Quality Supervisor: Perform first piece inspection and provide clearance for regular production.
  • Shift Engineer: Resolve any operational abnormalities and authorize rework or rejections.

 

4. Procedure

  1. शिफ्ट सुरू करताना मागील शिफ्टचा शेवटचा जॉब तपासणे:
    • इजेक्टर आणि कोर यंत्रणा व्यवस्थित चालू आहेत का? तपासा
    • डाय स्वच्छ करून, घट्टपणे बंद केलेली आहे का हे पहा
  2. प्लंजर लिकेज तपासणे
  3. लॅडल कोटिंग करणे (लॅडल कोटच्या सहाय्याने)
  4. होल्डिंग फर्नेसचे हिटर व मेटल टेंपरेचर तपासणे
  5. वॉटरबेस्ड डायकोट तयार करणे:
    • डायकोट : पाणी रेशियो = 2:200 (लिटर)
    • हे मिश्रण मशीन जवळील टँकमध्ये भरावे
    • प्रत्येक शॉटनंतर योग्य स्प्रे करावा
  6. गॅस बर्नरने डाय गरम करणे (150-180°C पर्यंत)
  7. रिजेक्टेड कास्टिंग रिजेक्शन बिनमध्ये ठेवणे
  8. फर्स्ट पीस इन्स्पेक्शन अहवाल मिळाल्यावरच प्रॉडक्शन सुरू करणे
  9. OK कास्टिंग, OK ट्रेमध्ये ठेवणे
  10. सुरुवातीचे OK कास्टिंग डायमेन्शनली तपासणे आणि व्हिज्युअल इन्स्पेक्शन करणे
  11. दोन किंवा अधिक व्हिज्युअल रिजेक्ट आढळल्यास त्वरित शिफ्ट इंजिनियरला कळवा
  12. कास्टिंग आयडेंटिफिकेशन कोड व कास्टिंग रिक्वायरमेंट चेक करणे
  13. मेटल टेंपरेचर 640–700°C दरम्यान असल्याशिवाय उत्पादन सुरू करू नये
    • पाच शॉट रिजेक्ट करून नंतरच OK ट्रेमध्ये ठेवावे
  14. ब्रेकनंतर (मेंटेनन्स/जेवण/चहा) पाच शॉट रिजेक्ट करूनच उत्पादन पुन्हा सुरू करावे
  15. मशीन बंद करताना शेवटचा शॉट मशीन टेबलवर ठेवावा
  16. शिफ्ट संपण्यापूर्वी मशीनच्या सभोवतालची जागा स्वच्छ ठेवावी

SOP for Pressure Die Casting (प्रेशर डाय कास्टिंग साठी सूचना)

1. Purpose
To establish a standardized procedure for starting and preparing Pressure Die Casting (PDC) machines to ensure safe, efficient, and defect-free operation.

 

2. Scope
This procedure applies to all PDC machine operators at V R ALUCAST prior to beginning any production activity.

 

3. Responsibilities

Machine Operator:
Ensure all pre-start checks and setup steps are followed accurately before running the machine.

Maintenance Staff:
Verify lubrication and mechanical condition of the machine components.

Shift Engineer:
Authorize startup after confirming that all parameters and settings are as per control plan.

 

4. Procedure

प्रेशर डाय कास्टिंग मशिन सुरू करताना खालील स्टेप्स फॉलो कराव्यात:

  1. प्रेशर डाय कास्टिंग मशीन चा मेन इलेक्ट्रिक पॅनल चालू करावा
  2. स्टॅबिलायझर व्होल्टेज लो असल्याची खात्री करावी
  3. मशीन कंट्रोल पॅनल वरील बुटींग होईपर्यंत थांबावे (2-3 मिनिटे)
  4. मशीन स्क्रीनवरील हायड्रोलिक ऑइल तापमान चेक करून घेणे
  5. मशीन चालू करण्यासाठी हायड्रोलिक ऑइल चे तापमान 40 डिग्री असल्याची खात्री करणे
  6. मशीन चालू करण्यापूर्वी मशीन मधील सर्व सेंट्रल लुब्रिकेशन हायड्रोलिक ऑइल, प्लंजर लुब्रिकेशन ऑइल लेवल्स, ऑइल इंडिकेटर मधून चेक करून घेणे
  7. मशीन चालू करण्यापूर्वी मशीनच्या कोणत्याही हलणाऱ्या पार्ट वरती टूल्स नसल्याची खात्री करून घेणे
  8. मशीन चालू करणे पूर्वी मशीन चे सर्व भाग स्वच्छ करून त्याला ऑइल लावून घेणे
  9. टायबार्स वरील मेटलचे तुकडे असल्यास स्वच्छ करून घेणे
  10. मशीनच्या सर्व हलणाऱ्या पार्ट्सना लुब्रिकेशन ऑइल लावले असल्याची खात्री करणे
  11. शॉट स्लीव्ह व्यवस्थितपणे फिक्स platen व डाय मध्ये बसते का याची खात्री करावी
  12. प्लंजर टीप ला लुब्रिकेशन होत असल्याची खात्री करावी
  13. मशीन चालू करण्यापूर्वी प्लंजर, मुव्हिंग platen होम पोझिशनला असल्याची खात्री करावी
  14. मेटल चे तुकडे मुवेबल बेडवर नसल्याची खात्री करावी
  15. डाय मशीन वर चढवण्यापूर्वी डाय ला लागणारे सर्व clamping एलिमेंट्स टेबलवर घ्यावे
  16. डाय clamping करण्यापूर्वी मशीन platens स्वच्छ करून घ्यावे
  17. डाय मशीन वर चढवण्यापूर्वी शॉट स्लीव्ह व प्लंजर चेक करून घ्यावे
  18. त्यानंतर कंट्रोल प्लॅन प्रमाणे डाय सेटिंग करून घ्यावे
  19. हायड्रोलिक नायट्रोजन एअर प्रेशर, कंट्रोल प्लान प्रमाणे आहे का याची खात्री करावी

SOP for Nitrogen Gas Filling and Checking
(नाइट्रोजन गॅस चेक करण्याची व भरण्याची पद्धत)

 

1. Purpose

To establish a standardized procedure for checking and filling nitrogen gas in machines to ensure proper functionality and safety.

 

2. Scope

This procedure applies to all machine operators at V R ALUCAST responsible for nitrogen gas filling and checking during production operations.

 

3. Responsibilities

  • Machine Operator: Follow each step in the procedure to ensure safe and proper filling of nitrogen gas.
  • Supervisor: Ensure that the procedure is followed correctly and verify that the gas filling is done safely.

 

4. Procedure

  1. नाइट्रोजन गॅस चेक करतेवेळी व भरतेवेळी मशीनचे मेन स्विच बंद असल्याची खात्री करावी.
  2. Accumulator ड्रेन करणे.
  3. मशीनमध्ये नाइट्रोजन किती आहे ते चेक करणे.
  4. जर नाइट्रोजन कमी असेल तर खालील पद्धतीप्रमाणे N2 भरणे:
    A. नाइट्रोजन गॅस सिलेंडर घेऊन त्याला पाइप फित करणे.
    B. नाइट्रोजन गॅस सिलेंडरमधील गॅस काचेची पारदर्शक बाटली उलटी धरून, ज्यामध्ये नाइट्रोजन गॅस लावलेल्या पाईपच्या साह्याने बाटलीमध्ये गॅस घेणे व त्यानंतर बाटलीचे तोंड बंद करून बाटली सरळ करणे.
    C. आगपेटीतील काडी पेटवून ती ज्योत बाटलीमध्ये सोडणे.
    D. आणि ज्योत विजल्यास नाइट्रोजन गॅस असल्याची खात्री होईल.
    E. नाइट्रोजन गॅस असल्याची खात्री झाल्यानंतर गॅस सिलेंडर पाईपच्या सहाय्याने मशीनला जोडणे व जोडण्यापूर्वी मशीनच्या नाइट्रोजन गेज जवळील व्हॉल्व बंद करणे.
    F. व्हॉल्व बंद झाल्याची खात्री करून बंद प्लग काढणे व पाईप जोडणे.
    G. पाईप जोडल्यानंतर गॅस सिलेंडरचा व्हॉल्व ओपन करा व नंतर गेज जवळील बंद केलेले व्हॉल्व चालू करणे व गरजेइतका नाइट्रोजन गॅस मशीनमध्ये भरणे.

SOP for Die Assembly / Disassembly
(डाय खोलने व जोडण्याचे नियम)

 

1. Purpose

To ensure the proper and safe assembly and disassembly of dies, preventing damage to parts and ensuring optimal performance.

 

2. Scope

This procedure applies to all die assembly and disassembly activities at V R ALUCAST.

 

3. Responsibilities

  • Machine Operator: Responsible for carrying out die assembly and disassembly correctly as per the procedure.
  • Maintenance Supervisor: Responsible for ensuring that all tools and safety measures are available and followed during the process.
  • Production Supervisor: Ensure that the assembly and disassembly is done on time and as per the standards.

 

4. Procedure

  1. डाय खोलताना ॲलन बोल्ट चे हेड स्लिप होणार नाही यासाठी योग्य साईजची ॲलन की वापरणे.
  2. इन्सर्ट खोलताना डाय चे सर्व बोल्ट निघाल्याची खात्री करणे.
  3. डाय खोलल्यानंतर त्याचे सर्व सब पार्ट ट्रेमध्ये व्यवस्थित ठेवणे.
  4. डाय ब्रेक डाऊन शीट प्रमाणे आवश्यक दुरुस्ती करणे. तसेच स्पेअर्स घेण्यापूर्वी त्याचे डायमेन्शनची खात्री करणे.
  5. दुरुस्ती केल्यानंतर पुन्हा सर्व बाजूंनी डायची खात्री करणे.
  6. ब्लू मॅचिंग चेक करणे. 0.05 mm च्या आत गॅप असावा.
  7. ब्ल्यू मॅचिंग ओके आल्यानंतर प्रोडक्शन साठी डाय इश्यू करणे.

SOP for Metal Cleaning – Degassing and Fluxing
(Degassing संबंधी चे नियम)

 

1. Purpose

To outline the proper method of degassing and fluxing molten metal to improve casting quality by removing entrapped gases and impurities.

 

2. Scope

This SOP applies to all furnace operators and production staff handling aluminum melt treatment at V R ALUCAST.

 

3. Responsibilities

  • Furnace Operator: Ensure all steps of degassing and fluxing are followed with appropriate safety and process discipline.
  • Shift Supervisor: Monitor the activity and verify proper execution of each step.

 

4. Procedure

  1. शिफ्ट सुरू करताना डी-गॅसिंग करणे गरजेचे आहे.
  2. Degassing किंवा इतर कोणत्याही कारणामुळे मशीन बंद राहिल्यास डाय पूर्णपणे बंद असणे आवश्यक आहे.
  3. मेटल डीगॅसिंग करताना प्रथम मेटलचे तापमान 640°C ते 700°C आहे का, याची खात्री करणे.
  4. Manual degassing unit वापरताना नायट्रोजन कंट्रोल व्हॉल्व व नायट्रोजन टाकीचा व्हॉल्व पूर्णपणे बंद असल्याची खात्री करणे.
  5. नायट्रोजन गॅस सर्क्युलर stainless steel pipe गरम करून, ती मेटलमध्ये हळूहळू बुडवणे.
  6. नायट्रोजन टाकीचा व्हॉल्व चावीच्या साहाय्याने हळुवारपणे उघडणे व कंट्रोल व्हॉल्वच्या साहाय्याने प्रेशर 2kg/cm² ते 5kg/cm² मध्ये सेट करणे.
  7. नायट्रोजन गॅस 5-10 मिनिटे मेटलमध्ये सोडणे.
  8. 10 मिनिटांनंतर नायट्रोजन कंट्रोल व टाकीचा व्हॉल्व बंद करून पाइप सुरक्षित ठिकाणी ठेवणे.
  9. गॅस पूर्णपणे बाहेर गेल्याची खात्री करून, 300kg furnace साठी 300gm फ्लक्स पावडर मेटलच्या पृष्ठभागावर पसरवणे.
  10. प्रत्येक 5 मिनिटांनी ड्रॉस बाजूला करत राहणे.
  11. ड्रॉस मेटल फ्री झाल्यानंतर झारीच्या सहाय्याने बाहेर काढणे व ड्रॉस पॅलेटवर पसरवणे.
  12. फर्नेसमधील सर्व ड्रॉस बाहेर काढल्याची खात्री करणे.
  13. मेटलवर तयार होणारे स्लज झारीच्या सहाय्याने बाहेर काढणे.

SOP for Job Inspection (जॉब तपासणीसाठी चे नियम)

 

1. Purpose

To establish a systematic procedure for inspecting jobs to ensure product quality and compliance with specifications.

 

2. Scope

This procedure applies to all jobs being inspected at V R ALUCAST.

 

3. Responsibilities

  • Machine Operator: Ensure that inspection is carried out as per the procedure and report any discrepancies immediately.
  • Quality Supervisor: Oversee the inspection process and ensure compliance with the procedure.
  • Production Supervisor: Ensure that corrective actions are taken when necessary.

 

4. Procedure

  1. जे जॉब चेक करायचे आहे त्याचे प्रोसेस इन्स्पेक्शन कंट्रोल प्लॅन घेणे.
  2. आपल्या इन्स्पेक्शन रिपोर्ट मधील डायमेन्शन्स हे टॉलरन्स प्रमाणे आहेत का याची खात्री करणे.
  3. इन्स्पेक्शन रिपोर्ट मधील सर्व डायमेन्शन्स ठरविलेल्या इन्स्ट्रुमेंट नुसार व्यवस्थित चेक करून नोंद करणे.
  4. एखादे डायमेन्शन, टॉलरन्स पेक्षा बाहेर असल्यास त्वरित मशीन बंद करणे व कॉलिटी अथवा प्रोडक्शन सुपरवायझरला सांगणे.
  5. वरील सर्व पॅरामीटर प्रत्येक दोन तासाला चेक करणे व नोंद करणे.
  6. व्हिज्युअल कास्टिंग डिफेक्ट्स ऑपरेटर्सनी प्रत्येक पंधरा मिनिटांनी व लाईन इन्स्पेक्टरने प्रत्येक तीस मिनिटांनी चेक करणे.
  7. ज्यात प्रॉब्लेम आहे त्या पॅरामीटर साठी मागील दोन तासांचे प्रोडक्शन जॉब अलग करून बाजूला ठेवणे व व्यवस्थित चेक करून ओके जॉब पुढे देणे व डिफेक्टिव्ह जॉब मेल्टिंग साठी देणे.
  8. डिफेक्टिव्ह पॅरामीटर करेक्शन करून ओके असल्याची खात्री करून घेणे मगच प्रोडक्शन सुरू करणे.
  9. प्रत्येक मशीनवर इन प्रोसेस रिपोर्ट शिफ्ट वाईज वेगवेगळा असावा.
  10. शिफ्ट संपल्यानंतर शिफ्टचे प्रोडक्शन इन प्रोसेस इन्स्पेक्शन रिपोर्ट रिमार्क इफ रिक्वायर्ड (कोअर पिन चेंज, डाय करेक्शन इत्यादी) भरून इन्स्पेक्शन आणि क्वालिटी सुपरवायझरची सही घेऊन फाइलिंग करणे.
  11. आपल्या ग्राहकाची तक्रार येऊ नये यासाठी वरील सूचनांचे पालन करणे.

SOP for Runner, Riser Cutting and Fettling
(रनर रायझर कटिंग व फेटलींग संबंधीच्या सूचना)

 

1. Purpose

To ensure proper runner, riser cutting, and fettling operations while maintaining casting quality and worker safety.

 

2. Scope

This procedure applies to all runner, riser cutting, and fettling activities at V R ALUCAST.

 

3. Responsibilities

  • Fettling Operator: Responsible for performing fettling, cutting, and inspection according to this procedure to maintain casting quality.
  • Quality Supervisor: Ensure that casting inspection is carried out effectively.

 

4. Procedure

  1. फेटलिंग करण्यापूर्वी कास्टिंग सुरुवातीला व्हिज्युअल इन्स्पेक्शन करून घेणे रिजेक्टेड कास्टिंग रिजेक्शन बीन मध्ये ठेवणे.
  2. रनर रायझर्स कट करताना कास्टिंग डॅमेज होऊ नये याची काळजी घेणे.
  3. सर्क्युलर ग्राइंडर वरील बेल्ट सुस्थितीत असल्याची खात्री करणे.
  4. फेटलिंग करतेवेळी सेफ्टी गॉगल्स, हँडग्लोब्स, शूज चा वापर करणे.

SOP for Final Job Inspection
(कास्टिंग दर्जा तपासण्यासाठी च्या सूचना)

 

1. Purpose

To ensure that all final castings are inspected as per the quality standards before dispatch to customers.

 

2. Scope

Applicable to all final inspection activities of aluminum castings at V R ALUCAST.

 

3. Responsibilities

  • Quality Inspector: Perform final inspection of castings, segregate OK and rejected parts, and ensure packing is done properly.
  • Quality Supervisor: Ensure procedure is followed and instruments are calibrated.

 

4. Procedure

  1. इन्स्पेक्शन करतेवेळी सर्व इन्स्ट्रुमेंट कॅलिब्रेटेड असल्याची खात्री करून घेणे.
  2. इन्स्ट्रुमेंट हाताळताना काळजी घेणे.
  3. फायनल क्वालिटी कंट्रोल प्लॅन प्रमाणे जॉब असल्याचे खात्री करणे.
  4. ओके पार्टस् आयडेंटिफाय करणे.
  5. रिजेक्टेड पार्ट्स रिजेक्टेड बीन मध्ये ठेवणे.
  6. ओके पार्ट्स करोगेटेड बॉक्स किंवा ट्रेमध्ये ठेवणे.
  7. पॅक झालेले बॉक्स किंवा ट्रे डिस्पॅच एरियामध्ये ठेवणे.

SOP for Packing
(पॅकिंग चे नियम)

1. Purpose

To ensure proper, clean, and correctly identified packing of all final inspected materials before dispatch.

 

2. Scope

Applicable to all packing activities of aluminum castings at V R ALUCAST.

 

3. Responsibilities

  • Packing Staff: Carry out packing activity as per instructions and maintain hygiene.
  • Quality Inspector: Ensure material is inspected and approved before packing.
  • Supervisor: Resolve queries and ensure correct tagging and documentation.

 

4. Procedure

  1. पॅकिंग साठी दिलेले मटेरियल फायनल इन्स्पेक्शन झालेले असल्याचे खात्री करून घेणे.
  2. पॅकिंग साठी लागणारे सर्व साहित्य एकत्रित करून घेणे.
  3. पॅकिंग करते पूर्वी मटेरियल स्वच्छ असल्याची खात्री करून घेणे.
  4. पॅकिंग करतेवेळी मटेरियल घाण होऊ नये याची काळजी घेणे.
  5. पॅकिंगच्या बाबतीत किंवा इतर कोणती शंका असल्यास सुपरवायझरला सूचना देणे.
  6. मटेरियल पॅकिंग झाल्यानंतर त्याच्यावरती आयडेंटिफिकेशन टॅग लावून घेणे.

SOP for Dispatch
(डिस्पॅच साठीचे नियम)

 

1. Purpose

To define the proper method for dispatching finished goods safely and accurately.

 

2. Scope

This procedure applies to all dispatch activities of aluminium castings from the V R ALUCAST premises.

 

3. Responsibilities

  • Dispatch Staff: Ensure material is verified, loaded safely, and dispatched as per schedule.
  • Security Personnel: Verify packed materials before vehicle exit.
  • Store Supervisor: Ensure correct invoicing and coordination.

 

4. Procedure

  1. पॅकिंग बॉक्स किंवा ट्रे मधील पार्टसची क्वांटिटी कन्फर्म करून इन्व्हाईस करायला देणे.
  2. इन्व्हॉईस झाल्यानंतर पॅकिंग बॉक्स किंवा ट्रे सिक्युरिटी कडून चेक करून घेणे.
  3. पॅकिंग बॉक्स किंवा ट्रे गाडीमध्ये काळजीपूर्वक लोड करणे.
  4. लोड करताना जॉब किंवा पार्ट्स डॅमेज होऊ नये याची खात्री करणे.

Control of Non-Conforming Products

                                                                                                                                                                                                    

1. Purpose

   To ensure that non-conforming products or services are identified, segregated, and managed appropriately.

 

2. Scope

   This procedure applies to all non-conforming products identified during production or inspection.

 

3. Responsibilities

   - Production Supervisor: Segregate and label non-conforming items.

   - Quality Department: Evaluate non-conformances and decide on corrective actions.

 

4. Procedure

   a. Identification and Documentation

      - Non-conforming products are immediately segregated and labeled.

      - A quality alert is generated to notify the team.

   b. Control and Segregation

      - Affected items are isolated from conforming inventory.

   c. Evaluation and Root Cause Analysis

      - Root cause analysis is conducted using 8D or fishbone diagram methods.

   d. Corrective Actions

      - Documented corrective and preventive actions are implemented and tracked.

Purpose

To define the color code assigned to each aluminium alloy grade used at V R Alucast, ensuring correct identification of material at all stages — receiving, storage, and production.

Scope

All aluminium alloy ingots received and used at V R Alucast, Ichalkaranji.

Color Code Chart

Sr. Aluminium Grade Color Code Usage
1 ADC12 GREEN Tag, mark, and store all ADC12 ingots with green color
2 A380 BLUE Tag, mark, and store all A380 ingots with blue color
3 ANSI360 BLACK Tag, mark, and store all ANSI360 ingots with black color
4 A383 YELLOW Tag, mark, and store all A383 ingots with yellow color
5 LM6 BROWN Tag, mark, and store all LM6 ingots with brown color
6 LM24 WHITE Tag, mark, and store all LM24 ingots with white color

Rules to Follow

  1. Every lot of ingots must be tagged with the correct color as soon as it is received and accepted.
  2. Color tag must remain visible on the lot at all times — in store and at the machine.
  3. Before issuing material to the machine, Production Supervisor must verify the color tag matches the grade required for the job.
  4. Operator must not use any material without a color tag. If tag is missing or unclear, stop and inform supervisor immediately.
  5. Different grades must never be stored together or mixed under any condition.
  6. If a new grade is introduced, it must be assigned a unique color and this document must be updated before use.
  7. Color tags or paint markers used must be clearly visible and not fade easily.

How to Apply Color Code

Method When to Use
Color tag / label tied to bundle Standard method for all incoming lots
Paint marker on ingot surface Additional marking for easy identification at machine
Color board displayed in store Reference display — one board per grade storage area
